label: Unrelated
research: The archival abstract identifies Jorgen Rosenberg as a shoemaker at Gehrden owing Ilsche Clases 15 Reichsthaler. The Brakel family account in ai_2026.json records Stephan Rosenberg from Gehrden in 1697, but the shared surname and locality do not establish a relationship to Jorgen; a separate local bearer remains possible. No supported family attribution can be made. The published Brakel household register records Henrich Rosenberg’s son Jürgen in 1654 and Hanß Jürgen in 1664, but neither entry identifies the Gehrden shoemaker or connects him to that household. The similar given name and contemporary dates make a link possible, not established: https://www.lwl.org/westfaelische-geschichte/txt/beitrwff-9453.pdf Gehrden’s parish registers add a likely local identification. On p. 80 the 1654 marriage record names Jürgen Rosenberg and Katharina Detzers, and p. 21 of the baptismal register names a Jürgen Rosenberg as godfather in 1671. The burial register p. 128 calls Georgius Rosenberg senior a former mayor of Gehrden in 1700. The baptisms of Georg’s son Jakob in 1663 and daughter Katharina in 1666 show a household already established in Gehrden while the Brakel list still places Henrich’s son in his household in 1664. The dates and name fit the cobbler, but the parish entries do not give his trade or connect this Gehrden household to Henrich’s Brakel family. Stephan’s 1697 move remains a link between the towns without establishing kinship. https://data.matricula-online.eu/de/deutschland/paderborn/DE_EBAP_12104/KB001-02-H/?pg=2, https://data.matricula-online.eu/de/deutschland/paderborn/DE_EBAP_12104/KB001-01-T/?pg=21 (see also pp. 15 and 17), https://data.matricula-online.eu/de/deutschland/paderborn/DE_EBAP_12104/KB001-04-S/?pg=21
